title: cross-layer-failure-taxonomy-and-healing-playbook-2026
content:
> **Archived 2026-11-15:** this page is superseded by "cross-layer-failure-taxonomy-and-healing-playbook-2028" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:
This playbook lays out a cross-layer failure taxonomy for the Redwood serving runtime together with a prioritized list of automated and manual healing patterns. Each failure class is linked to observable signals, rough SLO impact, kernel-scheduler interactions, and a simulation + benchmark protocol used to confirm a healing action works. The aim is lower MTTI and fewer customer-visible SLA breaches, while keeping actions explainable to on-call engineers.

Scope:
- Covered: serving runtime (scheduler, kernel plugins, KV cache, model swap path, request multiplexer), GPU nodes, and control-plane routing that affects inference.
- Not covered: cloud account-level provisioning failures and storage outages unrelated to KV cache persistence.

Key definitions:
1) Failure mode: a distinct root-cause class (kernel starvation, KV cache thrash, model swap oscillation).
2) Signal: a metric or event correlated with a failure mode (per-gpu-run-queue-latency, kernel-backpressure-count).
3) Healing pattern: an automated or manual mitigation (graceful model downgrade, preempt-and-slice, kernel rollback).

Cross-layer failure taxonomy:
- Hardware Degradation: NVLink flapping, thermal throttling, ECC escalations causing driver resets. Signals: gpu temperature > 85C sustained, nvlink_error_rate above baseline, driver-restart events. Impact: latency spikes, tail inflation, node pulled from pool.
- Kernel-level Regression / Latency Inflation: a new kernel with poor tiling for medium sequence lengths. Signals: kernel_duration_p50/p95 rise for a kernel id, kernel-inflight-queued, kernel-error-ratio. The scheduler responds with backpressure, raising queueing latency for all tenants.
- Scheduler Misconfiguration or Policy Conflict: fairness policy starving high-priority SLOs; priority inversion with plugins. Signals: queue-depth-by-priority, delayed-scheduler-invocations, starvation-duration>threshold.
- KV cache evictions & cold-start storms: bulk tenant traffic after a model swap causing churn and repeated warmups. Signals: kvcache-hit-rate drop, warmup-requests-per-minute spike.
- Model-variant oscillation: routing flipping between quantized and full-float variants on marginal quality regressions. Signals: model-switch-count, transient-quality-regression-alerts.
- Control-plane routing instability: region routing flaps, misapplied rollout policy, bad canary rules. Signals: route-change-events, sudden cross-region capacity shifts.

Severity matrix:
- Sev 1: sustained 50% increase in tail-99 latency, >5% error rate for >5 minutes.
- Sev 2: 20–50% tail-99 increase, transient errors on <5% of requests.
- Sev 3: within SLO but anomalous (local kernel bump, single-node throttling with failover).

Observable signals catalog:
- infra.*: gpu_temp_celsius, nvlink_errors, driver_restarts, node_oom_kills
- kernel.*: kernel_exec_time_ms{kernel_id}, kernel_error_count
- scheduler.*: queue_depth{priority}, time_to_schedule_ms, preemptions_per_minute
- kvcache.*: hit_rate, warmup_ops_per_minute, eviction_rate
- model.*: model_swap_count, variant_latency_ms, quality_regression_delta
- request.*: per_request_tail_latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, request_error_rate

Automated healing patterns (ordered by safety):
1) Protective throttling and admission control: when queue_depth{all} > Q_HI and p99_latency > L_HI, shed admission per tenant in 5–20% steps with exponential backoff.
2) Kernel safety-net rollback: trigger when kernel_exec_time_p95 exceeds baseline * 2.0 AND kernel errors increase. Flip the kernel feature flag back to the previous stable variant on the affected shard group, bump kernel-rollback-counter, notify runtime-ops. Confirm with a 10s microbenchmark on the canary path.
3) Model variant staged fallback: trigger when model_latency_multiplier > 1.5 OR kvcache-hit-rate < 0.2 for > 30s. Redirect new requests to a fallback variant with session preservation and quality sampling on the first 100 requests.
4) KV cache conservative mode & priming: shrink cache target for new sessions, prime top-N prefixes in the background, exempt high-SLA tenants from eviction until priming finishes.
5) Node isolation & graceful eviction: on persistent GPU errors or thermal limits, drain the node, transfer sessions where supported, block new allocations for 5 minutes, hand off to fleet-autorepair.
6) Scheduler quick-slice preemption (experimental): 50–100ms preemption slices to interleave low-latency tenants; flag-gated only.

Decision heuristics and guardrails:
- No model-variant fallback if quality monitoring shows >2% degradation in the last 30s.
- Kernel rollback needs at least one passing microbenchmark and an audit event with trace id.
- Admission-shed is tenant-scoped and rate-limited; global shed is emergency-only.

Manual triage and runbook (on-call):
1) Detection (0–5 minutes): open the SLO dashboard; check gpu_temp_celsius, driver_restarts, kernel errors, scheduler queue depth.
2) Containment (5–15 minutes): if noise, watch 5 more minutes; if persistent, enable tenant-scoped admission-shed at 20% and monitor p99.
3) Suspected kernel regression (15–30 minutes): runtime-admin rollback-kernel --shard-group <id> --cause "p95-regression-<id>", then bench-tool --target sh://<shard> --template warmup_short --duration 10s
4) KV cache storm (15–45 minutes): runtime-admin set-kvcache-mode --shards <list> --mode conservative; priming-svc start --strategy top-prefixes --window 10m
5) Escalate to runtime-core for cross-shard rollback or failed node isolation.

Kernel scheduling interactions:
- Preemption must avoid in-flight KV mutations; slice at request or token boundaries.
- Larger batches raise throughput but spread kernel regressions across tenants; use batch-size hysteresis to cut batch size quickly when p95 inflates.
- Alert on priority inversion when low-priority p95 improves while high-priority p95 worsens.

Simulation & validation recipe (required for new healing policies):
1) Harness: operational workload simulator with the blended-client-corpus, injecting thermal_increase, kernel_slowdown_x2, kvcache-eviction-spike.
2) Benchmarks: pre/post p95/p99 delta (5m steady state); tail amplification under 5% error injection; 1000 sampled completions for fallback quality.
3) Success criteria: healing must bring p99 to <=1.5x baseline within 180s for Sev2 and within 300s for Sev1, with quality inside policy bounds.
4) Regression check: no >0.5% error increase for unrelated tenants.

Release validation (Autonomous Recovery v1):
- Coordinates kernel-rollback, kvcache-conservative-mode and tenant-scoped admission-shed.
- Staged rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 5 days with automated rollback on SLO regressions.
- Each stage: 15m simulation run meeting success criteria.
- Rollback criteria: p99 regression > 1.5x baseline OR quality-sampling failure > 2% in two consecutive windows.

Telemetry additions:
- healing-events stream: healing_event{type, target, trigger, actor, trace_id}.
- healing_hint annotation on request traces.
- "Healing Effectiveness" dashboard (time-to-heal, success rate by type, per-tenant impact).

Ownership & escalation:
- Primary: eng-serving-runtime (pager: runtime-oncall@redwood.com).
- Secondary: eng-sre (pager: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.com).
- Path: on-call -> runtime-core -> infra-platform lead -> engineering director.

Appendix A — CLI snippets:
- runtime-admin rollback-kernel --shard-group sg-17 --kernel-id k-2026-08 --reason "p95_regression_20261003"
- runtime-admin set-kvcache-mode --shards sg-17,sg-18 --mode conservative --ttl 10m
- priming-svc start --strategy top-prefixes --sample-size 500 --shard sg-17

Appendix B — YAML policy sample:
  healingPolicies:
    - name: kernel-safety-net-v0
      conditions:
        - metric: kernel_exec_time_p95
          comparator: ">"
        - threshold: 2.0
      actions:
        - type: rollback-kernel
          cooldown: 120s
